source_refs.note: Topic 5.6.1, printed pages 104-105, as printed: the two factors as a list and Quick Check 5.5. The misprinted formulas in Quick Check 5.5 (e) are marked.

blocks.text: The factors affecting viscosity are as follows:

items: An increase of temperature increases the average kinetic energy of molecules. This allows the molecules to overcome the attractive forces. This lowers the viscosity.
The stronger the intermolecular forces, the greater the viscosity of liquids because liquid molecules cannot move around each other freely, so the resistance to flow increases.

blocks.prompt:
a) Arrange the following liquids is increasing order of surface tension, give reason:
Acetone (CH₃COCH₃), ethanol (C₂H₅OH), methoxy methane (dimethyl ether, CH₃OCH₃)
blocks.explanation: Order: CH₃OCH₃ < C₂H₅OH < CH₃COCH₃. Dimethyl ether (CH₃OCH₃) has no O−H, only weak dipole-dipole and London forces, and it is a gas at 20 °C (boiling point about −24 °C), so its surface tension is the lowest. Ethanol forms hydrogen bonds through its O−H, and the C=O of acetone is very polar and its molecule is larger. By Table 5.3, ethanol is 22.75 and acetone 23.70 (× 10⁻³ N m⁻¹): the two are close and acetone is slightly higher, because surface tension depends not only on hydrogen bonding but on the total intermolecular forces and the size of the molecule.

blocks.prompt: b) Why do you think tetracholro methane (carbon tetrachloride, CCl₄) has higher viscosity than chlroform (CHCl₃) but less than ethanol (C₂H₅OH)?
blocks.explanation: CCl₄ is a heavier, larger molecule than CHCl₃, so its London forces are stronger and it flows more slowly. Ethanol forms hydrogen bonds, which are stronger than the forces in either of these, so ethanol is the most viscous.

blocks.prompt: c) Drugs with higher viscosity are not oxidized easily, justify.
blocks.explanation: In a viscous liquid the molecules move slowly, so oxygen from the air diffuses in slowly and collides less often with the drug molecules. The rate of oxidation therefore stays low and the drug keeps longer.

blocks.prompt: d) The viscosity of honey is higher than water, explain why.
blocks.explanation: Honey is a very concentrated sugar solution. The large sugar molecules carry many O−H groups, which form many hydrogen bonds with one another and with water, so honey strongly resists flow.

blocks.prompt: e) Which of the following is more viscous: glycerine (CH₂OHCH₂OHCH₂OH) or hexane (C₆H₆)? Why?
blocks.explanation: Glycerine. Each of its molecules has three O−H groups that form many hydrogen bonds, while hexane has only weak London forces. (Correct formulas: glycerine CH₂OHCHOHCH₂OH, hexane C₆H₁₄; see the Book correction.)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In e) the formulas are misprinted. Glycerine (glycerol, propane-1,2,3-triol) is CH₂OHCHOHCH₂OH: the middle carbon carries one hydrogen, not two. Hexane is C₆H₁₄; C₆H₆ is benzene. Printed slips: 'is increasing order' → in increasing order; 'tetracholro' → tetrachloro; 'chlroform' → chloroform.
